articles.title_zh: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
facts_zh:
Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000
- Published
A framed lock of hair from America's first president, George Washington, has been sold at auction for $4,000 (£3,058).

The hair once belonged to John Gadsby, who entertained Washington in 1799 just before the latter's death the same year, and was later obtained by a collector called John K Lattimer from a descendent of Gadsby's, according to Richmond Auctions, which sold the item.
Its new owner has not been named.

all_titles.en: Lock of former US President George Washington's hair sells for $4,000

articles.title_zh: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
facts_zh:
FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
- Published
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.
The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.
It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US.

articles.title_zh: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
facts_zh:
Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
- Published
Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock, having run more than 24 hours into overtime as countries remain unable to agree on a new global climate deal.
In a late intervention on Friday, a group of countries led by France and Panama pushed back against the draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.
This still remains the main sticking point, along with a push from the Africa Group to get commitments on more money for adaptation - but the EU has previously said it would not support this.

all_titles.en: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock

facts_zh:
Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
- Published
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop.
He wants a reason to escalate".

articles.title_zh: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
facts_zh:
Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
- Published
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.
Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores was detained along with his lieutenant by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.
Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI.

articles.title_zh: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
facts_zh: Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground.
But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.

In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs , Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo.

articles.title_original: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
articles.title_zh: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
facts_zh:
Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
- Published
Denmark has accused Russian intelligence services of plotting to assassinate a Ukrainian-American near Copenhagen, saying they had "planned" and "initiated" the attempt.
Denmark's security and intelligence agency (PET) said it had stopped individuals who were intending to kill the person, named by Danish media as rapper Kyivstoner, at a concert in September.
Two people were charged with attempted murder and assisting a foreign intelligence service, and pleaded not guilty.

all_titles.en: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper

articles.title_original: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
articles.title_zh: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
facts_zh:
Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
- Published
A deal agreed between the UK and the European Union on Friday will come into force regardless of whether the two sides can negotiate a separate tuition fees agreement, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has told the BBC.
The measures agreed in Brussels include scrapping most checks on British food exports in return for the UK following some EU regulations from 2028, and a new youth mobility scheme.
However, a proposal from the bloc to lower the level of tuition fees paid by EU students in the UK has not been agreed.

all_titles.en: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says

articles.title_original: Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
articles.title_zh: Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
facts_zh:
Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
- Published
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Vladimir Putin is a "killer" in response to Donald Trump referring to the Russian leader as his "friend" in China this week.
Speaking to CNN, Zelensky said it was up to the US president "how to call Putin" but "for us, he is an enemy...
for us, he's a killer".

articles.title_original: Trafalgar Square Christmas tree felled in Norway
articles.title_zh: Trafalgar Square Christmas tree felled in Norway
facts_zh:
Trafalgar Square Christmas tree felled in Norway
- Published
This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.
The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old.
It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe.
